name: CI review as a GitHub App

pr.title: Post CI reviews as a GitHub App, and post Projector's own as Projector Review
pr.head: 2a4f35fed23dab9b645891e924f36aeecd201bdd

summary: Projector can review a pull request in a GitHub Actions job with no agent session running. The job runs project review run through the reusable action in actions/review/. Until now, those reviews posted with the workflow's own token, so they appeared as github-actions[bot]. Any workflow in the repository can post as that account, and the name says nothing about Projector.

This change lets the reviews post as a GitHub App, an account a person registers once and installs on their repositories. The action gains app-id and app-private-key inputs. When app-id is set, a new step uses the app's private key to mint a short-lived installation token, and the review posts as <slug>[bot] with that token. project init --ci-review --ci-app <slug> writes the setup, and Projector's own workflow switches to its projector-review app.

• Left for later: context repositories, the other feature an app token enables, stay deferred.
  • Unchanged: the summary job keeps the workflow's token, because it pushes refs/projector/summaries and the app token is read-only for contents.
  • Review status: both earlier findings are fixed, and the review of this head is clean, with three suggestions.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• App slug: the URL name of a GitHub App, such as projector-review. The app posts as <slug>[bot].
  • Installation token: a token GitHub issues to an app for the accounts it is installed on. It lasts an hour.
  • Composite action: an action made of steps, like actions/review/action.yml. The caller's env reaches every one of its steps, while its inputs set no environment variable.
  • review.reviewers: the logins whose Projector verdicts count beside the repository's own accounts.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• First review at c9c3725: changes requested. The private key reached every step of the action through the caller's env.
  • At 3f9b423 the key became an input that only the mint step reads, which settled that finding. That review requested changes because every plain init looked the recorded app up on GitHub and failed without it.
  • At 2a4f35f init --ci-app records the app's ID as review.ci_app_id, so a refresh needs no lookup. The review of this head is clean.
  • CI check and the repository's review.gate steps passed on this head.

groups.title: The action mints the app's token
groups.kicker: How a review job gets an app token and posts with it
intro: The reusable action actions/review/action.yml runs every CI review. With an app-id input, a new step, Mint the app's token, calls actions/create-github-app-token with the key from the app-private-key input. The token it mints reaches only the job's repository, with the same permissions the workflow grants its own token.

The key is an input rather than the caller's env on purpose. A caller's env reaches every step of a composite action, including the steps that install and run the agent. A composite action's inputs set no environment variable, so only the step that reads inputs.app-private-key gets the key.
The review step then uses the minted token as GH_TOKEN and names <slug>[bot] as PROJECTOR_TOKEN_LOGIN. It falls back to github.token and github-actions[bot] when no app is set.

files.note: Adds the app-id and app-private-key inputs and the mint step, and switches the review step's token and login to the app's.

checks.text: This is the only step that reads app-private-key, and neither workflow puts PROJECTOR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY under env. test_the_app_key_reaches_only_the_step_that_mints_its_token checks both, and it passed on this head.
The token and the login both come from the app step's outputs, so the review never posts as one account while naming another.

files.note: Tests the app workflow text, that only the mint step reads the key, the token and login wiring, and how init handles an app.

groups.title: init and ci-workflow write the app into the workflow
groups.kicker: The CLI flags, the workflow template, and the setting
intro: project init --ci-review --ci-app <slug> looks the app's numeric ID up with gh api apps/<slug>. It refuses an app GitHub does not show before it writes anything. It writes the ID into the workflow as app-id, passes the PROJECTOR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY secret as app-private-key, and records the slug as review.ci_app and the ID as review.ci_app_id. A later init rebuilds the same workflow from the recorded ID without asking GitHub, so it works offline. project review ci-workflow --app <slug> prints that same file.

init also puts <slug>[bot] in review.reviewers in place of github-actions[bot], so a workflow posting with its own token no longer counts as a reviewer. At a terminal, it asks for the path of the key file and has gh secret set read it as standard input, so the key never appears on a command line.
Only --ci-app looks the app up every time. When a slug is recorded without its ID and the lookup fails, a plain init warns, leaves the CI review as it is, and goes on, as its other GitHub calls do.

files.note: Adds --ci-app and --app, ci_app and app_id to find the app's ID, the reviewers rewrite, and set_app_key for the secret.

checks.text: A failed lookup stops init only when --ci-app was passed. Otherwise init warns and leaves the CI review as it is. test_a_later_init_refreshes_the_app_workflow_without_github_but_ci_app_still_asks_it and test_an_app_recorded_without_its_id_is_left_as_it_is_when_github_cannot_answer cover both paths, and CI check passed on this head.
This line drops only github-actions[bot]. A switch from one app to another leaves the old <slug>[bot] counted, which the review lists as a suggestion.

gh_lookup returns nothing on a 404, so app_id raises this refusal, and init --ci-app turns it into an error before it writes the workflow or records any setting. test_an_app_github_does_not_show_is_refused_before_anything_is_written covers it.

files.note: workflow_text takes an optional app ID and fills the template's @APP@ slot with the app-id and app-private-key inputs.
Adds the @APP@ slot before the review step's env:. With no app, it expands to nothing.
Registers review.ci_app as a string setting and review.ci_app_id as a whole number.

groups.title: Projector's own reviews post as Projector Review
intro: Projector's workflow passes app-id: '5827721' for the projector-review app, and the key secret as app-private-key. .projector.toml records the app and counts only projector-review[bot] as an extra reviewer. The key carries the app's authority over every installation, so the app stays installed only on the owner's repositories until a hosted token service replaces the secret.

files.note: Passes the app ID and the key secret to the action as inputs.
Records ci_app and ci_app_id, and replaces github-actions[bot] with projector-review[bot] in reviewers.

groups.title: Documentation and the plan
groups.kicker: How to set an app up, and what the plan records
intro: docs/review-in-ci.md gains a Post as a GitHub App section and rows for the app-id and app-private-key inputs. docs/cli.md describes the new flags and the review.ci_app and review.ci_app_id settings. The plan's § 9 records that the app input shipped before context repositories, why the ID is a setting rather than read from the workflow, and how Projector's own reviews post.

files.note: Says how to register the app, run init, and why the key is an input rather than env.
§ 9 records what shipped, including that the key is the app-private-key input § 2.4 names.
